Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 93, verses 1–2 (part 1 of 2):

It is Meccan according to the majority, and it was said to be Medinan.

Ibn al-Duraysi, al-Nahhas and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The surah 'By the night when it covers' was revealed in Mecca."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn al-Zubayr something similar.

al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan from Jabir ibn Samura, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite ﴿By the night when it covers﴾ and similar surahs in the Dhuhr and ʿAsr prayers."

al-Tabarani narrated in al-Awsat from Anas that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led them in the midday prayer (al-hajira), raised his voice, and recited ﴿By the sun and its brightness﴾ and ﴿By the night when it covers﴾. Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, were you commanded in this prayer with something?' He said: 'No, but I wanted to make it known to you.'" The hadith "Why did you not pray with ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾, ﴿By the sun and its brightness﴾, and ﴿By the night when it covers﴾" has already been mentioned.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "I say that this surah was revealed concerning generosity and stinginess: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾."

(p-1629) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying ﴿By the night when it covers﴾: that is, it covers with its darkness whatever was bright.

al-Zajjaj said: The night covers the horizon and everything between the heaven and the earth, so the light of day departs. It was said that it covers the day, and it was said that it covers the earth. The first is preferable.

﴿And the day when it becomes manifest﴾: that is, it appears, is revealed, and becomes clear, due to the removal of the darkness that was in the night, and that is by the rising of the sun.

﴿And He who created the male and the female﴾: here "mā" is the relative pronoun, meaning "and He who created the male and the female." He expressed "man" by "mā" to indicate the attributive sense and for the purpose of exalting: that is, and the Powerful, the Great, who created the two kinds, male and female.

al-Hasan and al-Kalbi said: its meaning is "and He who created the male and the female," so He would have sworn by Himself.

Abu ʿUbayda said: "wa-mā khalaqa" means "wa-man khalaqa" (and He who created).

Muqatil said: it means "and He created the male and the female," so "mā" in this case is a verbal-masdar particle (maṣdariyya).

al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: it means Adam and Eve, but the apparent sense is generality.

The majority read ﴿wa-mā khalaqa al-dhakara wa-l-unthā﴾, while Ibn Masʿud read "wa-l-dhakari wa-l-unthā" without "mā khalaqa".

﴿Indeed, your effort is diverse﴾: this is the answer to the oath: that is, indeed your deeds are varied: some of them are for Paradise, and some of them are for the Fire.

The majority of the exegetes said: "saʿy" is action. So one strives to free his soul, and one strives to destroy it. "Shattā" is the plural of "shatīt," like "marḍā" and "marīḍ." It was said that the varied is called "shattā" because of the distance between one part of it and another.

﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah﴾: that is, he spends his wealth in the ways of good and guards against the prohibitions of Allah that He forbade.

﴿And affirms the best [reward]﴾: that is, [believes in] the replacement from Allah.

The exegetes said: "As for he who gives" means he gives to those in hardship.

Qatada said: he gives the right of Allah that is upon him.

al-Hasan said: he gives sincerity from his heart. "And affirms the best" means: "There is no god but Allah," and this is what al-Dahhak and al-Sulami said.

Mujahid said: "the best" means Paradise.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: [it means] with prayer, zakat and fasting. The first is preferable.

Qatada said: "the best" means the promise of Allah which He promised that He would reward him.

al-Hasan said: [it means] the replacement for His giving. Ibn Jarir chose this.

﴿Then We will ease him toward ease﴾: that is, then We will prepare him for the good quality, which is doing good, and the meaning is: We will make easy for him the spending in the way of good and acting in obedience to Allah.

al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said: These verses were revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who bought six men from among the believers who were in the hands of the people of Mecca, who were torturing them for Allah.

﴿And as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient﴾: that is, he withholds his wealth and does not spend it in the paths of good, and "considers himself self-sufficient": that is, he renounces the reward and recompense, or he considers himself self-sufficient through the desires of this world from the bounties of the Hereafter.

﴿And denies the best [reward]﴾: that is, [denies] the replacement from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Mujahid said: [it means] Paradise. It was also narrated from him that he said: [it means] "There is no god but Allah."

﴿Then We will ease him toward hardship﴾: that is, We will prepare him for the quality of hardship, and We will facilitate it for him until the causes of good and righteousness become difficult for him, and he becomes weak in doing them, and that leads him to the Fire.

Muqatil said: It becomes difficult for him to give any good.

It was said: "al-ʿUsrā" is evil, because evil leads to punishment, and "al-ʿusra" is in punishment. The meaning is: We will prepare him for evil by making him act through his own hands.

al-Farraʾ said: "sa-nuyassiruhu" means "sa-nuhayyiʾuhu" (We will prepare him). The Arabs say: "qad yassarat al-ghanam" when they give birth or prepare for giving birth.

The poet said:
"They are two lords of ours, claiming [it], but they lead us only if their sheep have multiplied."

﴿And his wealth will not avail him when he falls﴾: that is, his wealth, which he withheld, will not avail him anything, or: what will avail him when he falls, that is, perishes. It is said: "radiya al-rajulu yardā radan" and "taraddā yatarradda," when he perishes.

Qatada, Abu Salih and Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿when he falls﴾ means when he falls into Hell. It is said: "radiya fi al-bi'r" and "taraddā," when he falls into it. And it is said: "Mā adrī ayna radiya," that is, where did he go?

﴿Indeed, to Us belongs guidance﴾: this sentence is a new sentence confirming what precedes it: that is, indeed, it is upon Us to explain.

al-Zajjaj said: It is upon us to show the path of guidance from the path of misguidance.

Qatada said: Upon Allah is the explanation: the explanation of what is forbidden by Him, of His obedience and of His disobedience.

al-Farraʾ said: Whoever follows guidance, the way is upon Allah, because of His saying: ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾ [al-Nahl: 9]. He says: whoever wants Allah, he is upon the straight path. al-Farraʾ also said: The meaning is: Indeed, to Us belongs guidance and misguidance, so he omitted "misguidance," like His saying: ﴿garments that protect you from the heat﴾ [al-Nahl: 81]. It was also said the meaning is: Indeed, upon Us is the reward of His guidance, which We have guided him to.

﴿And indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first [life]﴾: that is, to Us belongs everything in the Hereafter, and everything in this world, which We dispose of as We wish. So whoever wants both of them or one of them, let him seek it from Us. It was also said the meaning is: Indeed, for Us is the reward of the Hereafter and the reward of this world.

﴿So I have warned you of a Fire that blazes﴾: that is, I have cautioned and frightened you of a Fire that flares and blazes. Its origin is "tatalaẓẓā," but one of the two tāʾs was deleted for lightness.

ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, Yahya ibn Yaʿmar, and Talha ibn Musarrif read it according to the origin.

﴿None will burn therein except the most wretched﴾: that is, none will burn in it with a constant burning in the manner of eternity except the most wretched, who is the disbeliever. If others from among the sinners burn in it, their burning is not like his burning. What is meant by His saying "yaṣlāhā" is: he enters it, or he finds its burning, which is its heat.

Then He described the most wretched, saying: ﴿who denies and turns away﴾: that is, he denied the truth that the Messengers brought and turned away from obedience and faith.

al-Farraʾ said: "illā al-ashqā" (except the most wretched): except one who was wretched in the knowledge of Allah, may His praise be exalted.

He also said: He did not deny with an outright rejection, but he fell short of what he was commanded of obedience, so that was called denial, as you say: "Fulan met the enemy and denied" when he retreated and turned back from pursuing him.

al-Zajjaj said: This verse is the one for which the Murji'a (al-Irjaʾ) based their doctrine of irja' (deferral of judgment). They claimed that none enters the Fire except a disbeliever, and that the people of the Fire have degrees, among which the hypocrites are in the lowest level of the Fire.

Allah, glory be to Him, whatever He promised with a kind of punishment, it is fitting that He punishes with it. He said: (p-1630) ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [al-Nisa: 48]. So if everyone who did not associate partners were not punished, His saying "and He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills" would have no benefit.

Al-Zamakhshari said in al-Kashshaf: The verse is presented as a comparison between two states: a great one among the polytheists and a great one among the believers. It was intended to emphasize the two contrasting attributes. So it said "the most wretched," and made him specific to burning, as if the Fire had been created only for him. It said "the most pious," and made him specific to salvation, as if Paradise had been created only for him. It was also said that what is meant by "the most wretched" is Abu Jahl or Umayya ibn Khalaf, and by "the most pious" is Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.

The meaning of "sa-yujannabuhā al-atqā" (the most pious will be kept far from it) is: the one who guards against disbelief with complete guarding will be kept far from it.

al-Wahidi said: "al-atqā" is Abu Bakr al-Siddiq according to the saying of all the exegetes. End of quote. The more appropriate reading is to apply "al-ashqā" and "al-atqā" to everyone characterized by the two mentioned attributes. The meaning would be that none burns in it with a complete and constant burning except the one perfect in wretchedness, who is the disbeliever. And none is kept far from it and distanced from it with complete distance, such that he does not even approach it, let alone enter it, except the one perfect in piety. This does not contradict the entry of some sinful Muslims into the Fire in a non-constant way, nor the distancing of some who are not perfect in piety from the Fire in a distance that does not reach the level of distance of the one perfect in piety.

In summary: whoever among the Murji'a holds on to His saying ﴿None will burn therein except the most wretched﴾, claiming that "the most wretched" is the disbeliever because he is the one who denied and turned away, and denial did not occur from sinful Muslims, then it is said to him: What do you say about His saying ﴿and the most pious will be kept far from it﴾? It indicates that none is kept away from the Fire except the one perfect in piety. So whoever is not perfect in it, like sinful Muslims, is not among those kept away from the Fire. If you interpret "the most pious" in one of the ways of interpretation, it will bind you to the same for "the most wretched." So take this along with that, and be like the poet who said:
"I am content to bear love and come out of it neither against me nor for me."

It was also said that by "the most wretched" and "the most pious" is meant "the wretched" and "the pious," as Tarafa ibn al-ʿAbd said:
"Men wish that I die, and if I die, that is a path in which I will not be the only one."
That is, not the only one. It is not hidden from you that this contradicts describing "the most wretched" with denial, for that would only be from a disbeliever, so the purpose of the one who says this, that both attributes include sinful Muslims, is not achieved.

Then He, glory be to Him, mentioned the attribute of "the most pious," saying: ﴿who gives his wealth﴾: that is, he gives it and spends it in the ways of good. His saying "yatazakkā" (purifying himself) is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the subject of "yu'tī": that is, while he seeks to be pure in the sight of Allah, not seeking show-off or reputation. It is permissible for it to be a substitute (badal) for "yu'tī," included with it in the same grammatical role as the relative clause.

The majority read "yatazakkā," the present tense of "tazakkā." ʿAli ibn al-Husayn ibn ʿAli read "tazzakkā," with the assimilation of the tā' into the zāy.

﴿And none has upon him any favor to be repaid﴾: the sentence is a new sentence confirming what precedes it, that purification is done in the manner of sincerity, unmixed with anything that contradicts sincerity: that is, he is not one who gives his wealth in charity in order to repay someone's favor to him and reward him for it, but he seeks by his charity only the face of Allah, Exalted. The meaning of the verse is: there is no one among the people who has upon him a favor that is worthy of being repaid, such that he would intend by giving from his wealth to repay it. He said "tujzā" (is repaid) in the present passive, for the sake of the rhyme (fawāṣil); the original would be "yajzīhā iyyāhu" or "yajzīhi iyyāhā."

﴿Except seeking the countenance of his Lord, the Most High﴾: The majority read "ibtighāʾa" in the accusative. It may be accusative as an object of purpose (mafʿūl lahu) in meaning: that is, he gives only to seek the countenance of his Lord, the Most High. It may also be accusative as an object on the interpretation: that is, "I did not give you seeking your reward, but seeking the face of Allah." Yahya ibn Wathhab read it in the nominative as a substitute from the position of "niʿma" (favor); its position is nominative either as subject or as the topic (mubtada'), and "min" is extra. The nominative is the dialect of Tamim, because they permit substitution in the disconnected exception and treat it like the connected one.

Makki said: al-Farraʾ permitted the nominative for "ibtighāʾu" as a substitute from the position of "niʿma," but it is far-fetched.

Shihab al-Din said: It seems he was not aware of it as a reading, and his considering it far-fetched is itself far-fetched, for it is a widespread dialect. The majority also read "ibtighāʾa" with the long vowel, and Ibn Abi ʿAbla read it with the short vowel.

"Al-aʿlā" is an adjective for "rabb" (Lord).

﴿And he will surely be satisfied﴾: the lam is the one that introduces the oath: that is, "and by Allah, he will surely be satisfied with what We give him of honor and great reward."

The majority read "yarḍā" in the active voice, and it was also read in the passive voice.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 93, verses 1–2 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿By the night when it covers﴾, that he said: "When it grows dark."

Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Asakir narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) bought Bilal from Umayyah ibn Khalaf and Ubayy ibn Khalaf in exchange for a striped cloak and ten ounces (of silver), and he freed him for the sake of Allah. So Allah revealed: 'By the night when it covers' up to His saying: 'Indeed, your efforts are diverse' (the efforts of Abu Bakr, Umayyah and Ubayy), up to His saying: 'and denies the best,' (he said: 'the best' is) 'There is no god but Allah', up to His saying: 'We will ease him toward hardship,' (he said: 'hardship' is) the Fire."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah﴾, "from the wealth", "and is mindful of Allah", he said: "He fears his Lord." ﴿And believes in the best﴾, he said: "He believes in the replacement from Allah." ﴿We will ease him toward ease﴾, he said: "toward the good from Allah." ﴿But as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient﴾, he said: "He withholds his wealth and considers himself independent of his Lord." ﴿And denies the best﴾, he said: "(He denies) the replacement from Allah." ﴿We will ease him toward hardship﴾, he said: "toward evil from Allah."

Ibn Jarir narrated from him regarding "and believes in the best," that he said: "He is certain of the replacement."

Ibn Jarir also narrated from him: "﴿And believes in the best﴾" – he means: he believes in "There is no god but Allah." "﴿But as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient﴾" – he means: whom Allah has made wealthy, yet he withholds the zakat.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Asakir narrated from Amir ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: "Abu Bakr used to free (slaves) who had embraced Islam in Makkah. He would free old women and women when they embraced Islam. His father said to him: 'My son, I see you freeing weak people. If only you would free strong men who would stand with you, protect you and defend you.' He said: 'O father, I only want what is with Allah.' (Amir) said: '(p-1631) One of the people of my household told me that this verse was revealed concerning him: ﴿As for he who gives and fears (Allah)﴾, ﴿and believes in the best﴾, ﴿We will ease him toward ease﴾.'"

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿As for he who gives and fears (Allah)﴾, ﴿and believes in the best﴾, that he said: "(It refers to) Abu Bakr al-Siddiq." ﴿But as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient﴾, ﴿and denies the best﴾, that he said: "(It refers to) Abu Sufyan ibn Harb."

Al-Bukhari, Muslim, the authors of the Sunan and others narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: "We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) at a funeral. He said: 'There is none among you but that his place in Paradise and his place in the Fire has been written.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, should we not then rely (on that)?' He said: 'Act, for each person is made easy for that for which he was created. As for the one who is among the people of happiness, he will be made easy for the deeds of the people of happiness, and as for the one who is among the people of wretchedness, he will be made easy for the deeds of the people of wretchedness.' Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears (Allah)﴾, ﴿and believes in the best﴾, up to His saying: ﴿toward hardship﴾."

Ahmad, Muslim and others narrated from Jabir ibn Abdullah that Suraqah ibn Malik said: "O Messenger of Allah, for what should we work? For something whose decrees have been settled and the pens have dried, or for something in which work is yet to be done?" He said: "Rather, for something whose decrees have been settled and the pens have dried." Suraqah said: "Then why work, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Act, for each person is made easy for that for which he was created." And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿As for he who gives and fears (Allah)﴾, up to His saying: ﴿We will ease him toward hardship﴾. (32)

The hadith of Imran ibn Husayn has already been mentioned in the surah before this one. There are also hadiths on this subject through a number of the Companions.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "You will surely enter Paradise, except for those who refuse." They said: "And who would refuse to enter Paradise?" Then he recited (the verse): ﴿He denied and turned away﴾.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Umamah, who said: "None of this Ummah will remain but that Allah will admit him into Paradise, except one who runs away from Allah as a bad camel runs away from its owners. Whoever does not believe me, then Allah says: ﴿None will enter it except the most wretched, who denied and turned away﴾," (meaning) he denied what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought and turned away from it.

Ahmad, al-Hakim and al-Diya' narrated from Abu Umamah al-Bahili that he was asked about the gentlest word he had heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Surely all of you will be admitted into Paradise by Allah, except one who runs away from Allah as a camel runs away from its owners.'"

Ahmad, Ibn Majah and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "None enters the Fire except the wretched one." It was said: "And who is the wretched one?" He said: "The one who does not perform any act of obedience to Allah and does not abandon any act of disobedience to Allah."

Ahmad and al-Bukhari narrated from him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "All of my Ummah will enter Paradise on the Day of Resurrection, except the one who refuses." They said: "And who would refuse, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Whoever obeys me enters Paradise, and whoever disobeys me has refused."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Urwah that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq freed seven (slaves), all of whom were tortured for the sake of Allah: Bilal, Amir ibn Fuhayrah, al-Nahdiyyah and her daughter, Zinnirah, Umm Isa, and the slave-girl of the Banu al-Mu'ammal. And concerning him was revealed: ﴿But the most righteous will be spared it﴾, up to the end of the surah.

Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, narrated from Amir ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr what we have mentioned earlier from him, but he added to it: "So this verse was revealed concerning him: ﴿As for he who gives and fears (Allah)﴾, up to His saying: ﴿and no one has any favor for which he should be recompensed, except seeking the Face of his Lord, the Most High. And he is going to be satisfied.﴾"

Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated similar to this from him by another route.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿But the most righteous will be spared it﴾, that he said: "He is Abu Bakr al-Siddiq."

al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said: These verses were revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who bought six men from among the believers who were in the hands of the people of Mecca, who were torturing them for Allah.

﴿And as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient﴾: that is, he withholds his wealth and does not spend it in the paths of good, and "considers himself self-sufficient": that is, he renounces the reward and recompense, or he considers himself self-sufficient through the desires of this world from the bounties of the Hereafter.

﴿And denies the best [reward]﴾: that is, [denies] the replacement from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Mujahid said: [it means] Paradise. It was also narrated from him that he said: [it means] "There is no god but Allah."

﴿Then We will ease him toward hardship﴾: that is, We will prepare him for the quality of hardship, and We will facilitate it for him until the causes of good and righteousness become difficult for him, and he becomes weak in doing them, and that leads him to the Fire.

Muqatil said: It becomes difficult for him to give any good.

It was said: "al-ʿUsrā" is evil, because evil leads to punishment, and "al-ʿusra" is in punishment. The meaning is: We will prepare him for evil by making him act through his own hands.

al-Farraʾ said: "sa-nuyassiruhu" means "sa-nuhayyiʾuhu" (We will prepare him). The Arabs say: "qad yassarat al-ghanam" when they give birth or prepare for giving birth.

The poet said:
"They are two lords of ours, claiming [it], but they lead us only if their sheep have multiplied."

﴿And his wealth will not avail him when he falls﴾: that is, his wealth, which he withheld, will not avail him anything, or: what will avail him when he falls, that is, perishes. It is said: "radiya al-rajulu yardā radan" and "taraddā yatarradda," when he perishes.

Qatada, Abu Salih and Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿when he falls﴾ means when he falls into Hell. It is said: "radiya fi al-bi'r" and "taraddā," when he falls into it. And it is said: "Mā adrī ayna radiya," that is, where did he go?

﴿Indeed, to Us belongs guidance﴾: this sentence is a new sentence confirming what precedes it: that is, indeed, it is upon Us to explain.

al-Zajjaj said: It is upon us to show the path of guidance from the path of misguidance.

Qatada said: Upon Allah is the explanation: the explanation of what is forbidden by Him, of His obedience and of His disobedience.

al-Farraʾ said: Whoever follows guidance, the way is upon Allah, because of His saying: ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾ [al-Nahl: 9]. He says: whoever wants Allah, he is upon the straight path. al-Farraʾ also said: The meaning is: Indeed, to Us belongs guidance and misguidance, so he omitted "misguidance," like His saying: ﴿garments that protect you from the heat﴾ [al-Nahl: 81]. It was also said the meaning is: Indeed, upon Us is the reward of His guidance, which We have guided him to.

﴿And indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first [life]﴾: that is, to Us belongs everything in the Hereafter, and everything in this world, which We dispose of as We wish. So whoever wants both of them or one of them, let him seek it from Us. It was also said the meaning is: Indeed, for Us is the reward of the Hereafter and the reward of this world.

﴿So I have warned you of a Fire that blazes﴾: that is, I have cautioned and frightened you of a Fire that flares and blazes. Its origin is "tatalaẓẓā," but one of the two tāʾs was deleted for lightness.

ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, Yahya ibn Yaʿmar, and Talha ibn Musarrif read it according to the origin.

﴿None will burn therein except the most wretched﴾: that is, none will burn in it with a constant burning in the manner of eternity except the most wretched, who is the disbeliever. If others from among the sinners burn in it, their burning is not like his burning. What is meant by His saying "yaṣlāhā" is: he enters it, or he finds its burning, which is its heat.

Then He described the most wretched, saying: ﴿who denies and turns away﴾: that is, he denied the truth that the Messengers brought and turned away from obedience and faith.

al-Farraʾ said: "illā al-ashqā" (except the most wretched): except one who was wretched in the knowledge of Allah, may His praise be exalted.

He also said: He did not deny with an outright rejection, but he fell short of what he was commanded of obedience, so that was called denial, as you say: "Fulan met the enemy and denied" when he retreated and turned back from pursuing him.

al-Zajjaj said: This verse is the one for which the Murji'a (al-Irjaʾ) based their doctrine of irja' (deferral of judgment). They claimed that none enters the Fire except a disbeliever, and that the people of the Fire have degrees, among which the hypocrites are in the lowest level of the Fire.

Allah, glory be to Him, whatever He promised with a kind of punishment, it is fitting that He punishes with it. He said: (p-1630) ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [al-Nisa: 48]. So if everyone who did not associate partners were not punished, His saying "and He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills" would have no benefit.

Al-Zamakhshari said in al-Kashshaf: The verse is presented as a comparison between two states: a great one among the polytheists and a great one among the believers. It was intended to emphasize the two contrasting attributes. So it said "the most wretched," and made him specific to burning, as if the Fire had been created only for him. It said "the most pious," and made him specific to salvation, as if Paradise had been created only for him. It was also said that what is meant by "the most wretched" is Abu Jahl or Umayya ibn Khalaf, and by "the most pious" is Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.

The meaning of "sa-yujannabuhā al-atqā" (the most pious will be kept far from it) is: the one who guards against disbelief with complete guarding will be kept far from it.

al-Wahidi said: "al-atqā" is Abu Bakr al-Siddiq according to the saying of all the exegetes. End of quote. The more appropriate reading is to apply "al-ashqā" and "al-atqā" to everyone characterized by the two mentioned attributes. The meaning would be that none burns in it with a complete and constant burning except the one perfect in wretchedness, who is the disbeliever. And none is kept far from it and distanced from it with complete distance, such that he does not even approach it, let alone enter it, except the one perfect in piety. This does not contradict the entry of some sinful Muslims into the Fire in a non-constant way, nor the distancing of some who are not perfect in piety from the Fire in a distance that does not reach the level of distance of the one perfect in piety.

In summary: whoever among the Murji'a holds on to His saying ﴿None will burn therein except the most wretched﴾, claiming that "the most wretched" is the disbeliever because he is the one who denied and turned away, and denial did not occur from sinful Muslims, then it is said to him: What do you say about His saying ﴿and the most pious will be kept far from it﴾? It indicates that none is kept away from the Fire except the one perfect in piety. So whoever is not perfect in it, like sinful Muslims, is not among those kept away from the Fire. If you interpret "the most pious" in one of the ways of interpretation, it will bind you to the same for "the most wretched." So take this along with that, and be like the poet who said:
"I am content to bear love and come out of it neither against me nor for me."

It was also said that by "the most wretched" and "the most pious" is meant "the wretched" and "the pious," as Tarafa ibn al-ʿAbd said:
"Men wish that I die, and if I die, that is a path in which I will not be the only one."
That is, not the only one. It is not hidden from you that this contradicts describing "the most wretched" with denial, for that would only be from a disbeliever, so the purpose of the one who says this, that both attributes include sinful Muslims, is not achieved.

Then He, glory be to Him, mentioned the attribute of "the most pious," saying: ﴿who gives his wealth﴾: that is, he gives it and spends it in the ways of good. His saying "yatazakkā" (purifying himself) is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the subject of "yu'tī": that is, while he seeks to be pure in the sight of Allah, not seeking show-off or reputation. It is permissible for it to be a substitute (badal) for "yu'tī," included with it in the same grammatical role as the relative clause.

The majority read "yatazakkā," the present tense of "tazakkā." ʿAli ibn al-Husayn ibn ʿAli read "tazzakkā," with the assimilation of the tā' into the zāy.

﴿And none has upon him any favor to be repaid﴾: the sentence is a new sentence confirming what precedes it, that purification is done in the manner of sincerity, unmixed with anything that contradicts sincerity: that is, he is not one who gives his wealth in charity in order to repay someone's favor to him and reward him for it, but he seeks by his charity only the face of Allah, Exalted. The meaning of the verse is: there is no one among the people who has upon him a favor that is worthy of being repaid, such that he would intend by giving from his wealth to repay it. He said "tujzā" (is repaid) in the present passive, for the sake of the rhyme (fawāṣil); the original would be "yajzīhā iyyāhu" or "yajzīhi iyyāhā."

﴿Except seeking the countenance of his Lord, the Most High﴾: The majority read "ibtighāʾa" in the accusative. It may be accusative as an object of purpose (mafʿūl lahu) in meaning: that is, he gives only to seek the countenance of his Lord, the Most High. It may also be accusative as an object on the interpretation: that is, "I did not give you seeking your reward, but seeking the face of Allah." Yahya ibn Wathhab read it in the nominative as a substitute from the position of "niʿma" (favor); its position is nominative either as subject or as the topic (mubtada'), and "min" is extra. The nominative is the dialect of Tamim, because they permit substitution in the disconnected exception and treat it like the connected one.

Makki said: al-Farraʾ permitted the nominative for "ibtighāʾu" as a substitute from the position of "niʿma," but it is far-fetched.

Shihab al-Din said: It seems he was not aware of it as a reading, and his considering it far-fetched is itself far-fetched, for it is a widespread dialect. The majority also read "ibtighāʾa" with the long vowel, and Ibn Abi ʿAbla read it with the short vowel.

"Al-aʿlā" is an adjective for "rabb" (Lord).

﴿And he will surely be satisfied﴾: the lam is the one that introduces the oath: that is, "and by Allah, he will surely be satisfied with what We give him of honor and great reward."

The majority read "yarḍā" in the active voice, and it was also read in the passive voice.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 93, verses 1–2 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿By the night when it covers﴾, that he said: "When it grows dark."

Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Asakir narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) bought Bilal from Umayyah ibn Khalaf and Ubayy ibn Khalaf in exchange for a striped cloak and ten ounces (of silver), and he freed him for the sake of Allah. So Allah revealed: 'By the night when it covers' up to His saying: 'Indeed, your efforts are diverse' (the efforts of Abu Bakr, Umayyah and Ubayy), up to His saying: 'and denies the best,' (he said: 'the best' is) 'There is no god but Allah', up to His saying: 'We will ease him toward hardship,' (he said: 'hardship' is) the Fire."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah﴾, "from the wealth", "and is mindful of Allah", he said: "He fears his Lord." ﴿And believes in the best﴾, he said: "He believes in the replacement from Allah." ﴿We will ease him toward ease﴾, he said: "toward the good from Allah." ﴿But as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient﴾, he said: "He withholds his wealth and considers himself independent of his Lord." ﴿And denies the best﴾, he said: "(He denies) the replacement from Allah." ﴿We will ease him toward hardship﴾, he said: "toward evil from Allah."

Ibn Jarir narrated from him regarding "and believes in the best," that he said: "He is certain of the replacement."

Ibn Jarir also narrated from him: "﴿And believes in the best﴾" – he means: he believes in "There is no god but Allah." "﴿But as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient﴾" – he means: whom Allah has made wealthy, yet he withholds the zakat.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Asakir narrated from Amir ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: "Abu Bakr used to free (slaves) who had embraced Islam in Makkah. He would free old women and women when they embraced Islam. His father said to him: 'My son, I see you freeing weak people. If only you would free strong men who would stand with you, protect you and defend you.' He said: 'O father, I only want what is with Allah.' (Amir) said: '(p-1631) One of the people of my household told me that this verse was revealed concerning him: ﴿As for he who gives and fears (Allah)﴾, ﴿and believes in the best﴾, ﴿We will ease him toward ease﴾.'"

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿As for he who gives and fears (Allah)﴾, ﴿and believes in the best﴾, that he said: "(It refers to) Abu Bakr al-Siddiq." ﴿But as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient﴾, ﴿and denies the best﴾, that he said: "(It refers to) Abu Sufyan ibn Harb."

Al-Bukhari, Muslim, the authors of the Sunan and others narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: "We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) at a funeral. He said: 'There is none among you but that his place in Paradise and his place in the Fire has been written.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, should we not then rely (on that)?' He said: 'Act, for each person is made easy for that for which he was created. As for the one who is among the people of happiness, he will be made easy for the deeds of the people of happiness, and as for the one who is among the people of wretchedness, he will be made easy for the deeds of the people of wretchedness.' Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears (Allah)﴾, ﴿and believes in the best﴾, up to His saying: ﴿toward hardship﴾."

Ahmad, Muslim and others narrated from Jabir ibn Abdullah that Suraqah ibn Malik said: "O Messenger of Allah, for what should we work? For something whose decrees have been settled and the pens have dried, or for something in which work is yet to be done?" He said: "Rather, for something whose decrees have been settled and the pens have dried." Suraqah said: "Then why work, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Act, for each person is made easy for that for which he was created." And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿As for he who gives and fears (Allah)﴾, up to His saying: ﴿We will ease him toward hardship﴾. (32)

The hadith of Imran ibn Husayn has already been mentioned in the surah before this one. There are also hadiths on this subject through a number of the Companions.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "You will surely enter Paradise, except for those who refuse." They said: "And who would refuse to enter Paradise?" Then he recited (the verse): ﴿He denied and turned away﴾.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Umamah, who said: "None of this Ummah will remain but that Allah will admit him into Paradise, except one who runs away from Allah as a bad camel runs away from its owners. Whoever does not believe me, then Allah says: ﴿None will enter it except the most wretched, who denied and turned away﴾," (meaning) he denied what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought and turned away from it.

Ahmad, al-Hakim and al-Diya' narrated from Abu Umamah al-Bahili that he was asked about the gentlest word he had heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Surely all of you will be admitted into Paradise by Allah, except one who runs away from Allah as a camel runs away from its owners.'"

Ahmad, Ibn Majah and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "None enters the Fire except the wretched one." It was said: "And who is the wretched one?" He said: "The one who does not perform any act of obedience to Allah and does not abandon any act of disobedience to Allah."

Ahmad and al-Bukhari narrated from him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "All of my Ummah will enter Paradise on the Day of Resurrection, except the one who refuses." They said: "And who would refuse, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Whoever obeys me enters Paradise, and whoever disobeys me has refused."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Urwah that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq freed seven (slaves), all of whom were tortured for the sake of Allah: Bilal, Amir ibn Fuhayrah, al-Nahdiyyah and her daughter, Zinnirah, Umm Isa, and the slave-girl of the Banu al-Mu'ammal. And concerning him was revealed: ﴿But the most righteous will be spared it﴾, up to the end of the surah.

Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, narrated from Amir ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr what we have mentioned earlier from him, but he added to it: "So this verse was revealed concerning him: ﴿As for he who gives and fears (Allah)﴾, up to His saying: ﴿and no one has any favor for which he should be recompensed, except seeking the Face of his Lord, the Most High. And he is going to be satisfied.﴾"

Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated similar to this from him by another route.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿But the most righteous will be spared it﴾, that he said: "He is Abu Bakr al-Siddiq."

This surah is Meccan, without any dispute.

Ibn al-Durays, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas: "It was revealed when al-Duha (the forenoon) was in Mecca."

al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated through Abu al-Hasan al-Muqri, who said: I heard Ikrimah ibn Sulayman say: "I recited to Isma'il ibn Qustutin, and when I reached 'Wal-Duha' (﴿Wal-Duha﴾) he said: 'Glorify (takbir) until you finish.' 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir informed him that he had recited to Mujahid, and he ordered him to do so."

Mujahid informed him that Ibn Abbas had ordered him to do so.

Ibn Abbas informed him that Ubayy ibn Ka'b had ordered him to do so.

Ubayy informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had ordered him to do so.

Abu al-Hasan al-Muqri mentioned above is Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Bazzah al-Muqri.

Ibn Kathir said: "This is a sunnah which Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Bazzi, from the descendants of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, was alone in narrating. He was an imam in the readings (qira'at)."

As for in hadith, Abu Hatim al-Razi weakened him and said: "I did not take from him." Likewise Abu Ja'far al-cUqayli said: "He is munkar al-hadith (rejected in narration)."

Ibn Kathir said: "Then the reciters differed about the place of this takbir and its manner. Some of them said: it is glorified from the end of the night when it covers (wa'l-layli idha yaghsha); others said: from the end of al-Duha."

The manner of the takbir according to some of them is that one says: "Allahu akbar" and stops. Among them are those who say: "Allahu akbar, la ilaha illa Allah, Allahu akbar."

They mention, regarding the occasion of the takbir from the beginning of al-Duha, that when revelation was delayed from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and paused for that period, then the angel came and revealed to him "Wal-Duha, wal-layli idha saja" (the surah), and he glorified (Allah) out of joy and happiness. But they did not narrate this with a chain by which it can be judged sound or weak.

al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Jundub al-Bajali, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ fell ill and did not rise for the night for two or three nights. A woman came to him and said: 'O Muhammad, I do not see your devil except that he has left you; he has not come near you for two or three nights.' So Allah revealed: 'Wal-Duha, wal-layli idha saja, ma wadda'aka rabbuka wa ma qala' (﴿Wal-Duha﴾ ﴿wal-layli idha saja﴾ ﴿ma wadda'aka rabbuka wa ma qala﴾)."

al-Firyabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Jundub, who said: "Jibril was delayed from the Prophet ﷺ, so the polytheists said: 'Muhammad has been abandoned,' and then there was revealed: 'Ma wadda'aka rabbuka wa ma qala' (﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He become displeased.﴾)."

al-Tabarani narrated from Jundub, who said: "Jibril was held back from the Prophet ﷺ, and some of his paternal cousins' daughters said: 'I do not see your companion except that he has become displeased with you,' so there was revealed: 'Wal-Duha' (﴿By the morning brightness﴾)."

al-Tirmidhi, who declared it sound, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Jundub, and in it: a woman said to him: "I do not see your devil except that he has left you," so there was revealed: "Wal-Duha" (p-1632).

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Here al-Duha means the whole of the daytime.

Due to His saying: ﴿wal-layli idha saja﴾ (﴿By the night when it covers﴾). When He contrasted al-Duha with the night, this indicates that what is meant by it is the entire day, not part of it.

It is in origin a name for the time when the sun rises high, as was mentioned earlier in His saying: ﴿wash-shamsi wa duhaha﴾ (﴿By the sun and its brightness﴾). The apparent meaning is that what is meant is al-Duha without specification.

Qatadah, Muqatil and Ja'far al-Sadiq said: what is meant by it is the forenoon in which Allah spoke to Musa, and what is meant by His saying ﴿wal-layli idha saja﴾ is the night of the Mi'raj. It was also said that what is meant by al-Duha is the hour in which the magicians fell down prostrating, as in His saying: ﴿wa an yuhsharan-nasu duha﴾ (﴿and that the people be gathered in the forenoon﴾) [Ta-Ha: 59]. It was also said that the sworn-by thing has an implied omitted noun, as was mentioned earlier in its parallels: that is, "by the Lord of al-Duha." It was also said its estimate is: "and by the brightness of al-Duha," but there is no basis for this, for Allah the Exalted may swear by whatever He wills of His creation. It was also said: al-Duha is the light of Paradise and al-layl is the darkness of Hell; it was also said al-Duha is the light of the hearts of the knowers and al-layl is the blackness of the hearts of the disbelievers.

﴿wal-layli idha saja﴾ means: became still. Thus said Qatadah, Mujahid, Ibn Zayd, Ikrimah and others: one says "laylatun sajiyah," meaning a still night, and one says of an eye when its gaze becomes still that it is sajiyah. One says: saja al-shay'u yasju sujuwwan, when it became still.

Ata said: saja means when it was covered with majesty.

Thalab narrated from Ibn al-A'rabi: saja means its darkness extended.

al-Asma'i said: the sujuww of the night is its covering of the day, like a man being covered with a garment.

al-Hasan said: it covered with its darkness.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it came forward.

Mujahid also said: it leveled out. The first is preferable, and it is the view of the majority of the exegetes and the lexicographers.

The meaning of its stillness is the settling and leveling of its darkness, so that nothing is added to it after that.

﴿ma wadda'aka rabbuka﴾ This is the answer to the oath: that is, your Lord has not cut you off as one who bids farewell. The majority read ﴿ma wadda'aka﴾ with the dal doubled, from tawdi' (bidding farewell), which is the farewell of one departing. Ibn Abbas, Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Ibn Hashim, Ibn Abi Ablah and Abu Haywah read it with the dal lightened, from their saying wada'ahu, meaning he left him. From this is the poet's saying:

"Ask my amir what changed him from my union today, until he left him."

Tawdi' is more emphatic in farewell, for whoever bids you farewell while departing has gone far in abandoning you.

al-Mubarrad said: they hardly say wada'a nor wadhara, because of the weakness of the waw when it is put first, and they dispensed with it by tarak (he left).

Abu Ubayda said: wadda'aka is from tawdi', as one who bids farewell takes leave.

al-Zajjaj said: He did not cut off the revelation. We have already mentioned the cause of revelation of this verse at the beginning of this surah.

﴿wa ma qala﴾ al-qila means hatred; one says qalahu, yaqlihi, qila'.

al-Zajjaj said: and He did not hate you. He said ﴿wa ma qala﴾ and did not say wa ma qalaka, for agreement with the ends of the verses. The meaning: and He did not hate you. From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

"I am not one who hates the friends, nor one who hates."

﴿wa lal-akhiratu khayrun laka mina al-ula﴾ The lam is the answer to a omitted oath: that is, Paradise is better for you than this world, even though he ﷺ was given in this world of the nobility of prophethood what makes every nobility small in comparison and every honour in this world diminish in relation to it. But since this world in its entirety is mixed with troubles and disturbed by human accidents, and life in it is like the dreams of a sleeper or a passing shadow, it is nothing in relation to the Hereafter; and since it is a path to the Hereafter and a cause of attaining what Allah has prepared for His righteous servants of great good, through the deeds performed in it which necessitate winning Paradise, it has some good in it in general from this aspect.

﴿wa la-sawfa yu'tika rabbuka fa-tarda﴾ This lam — it was said it is the lam of the beginning, entering on the predicate to emphasize the content of the sentence, and the subject is omitted, its estimate being "wa la-anta sawfa yu'tika" etc. It is not the lam of oath, because it does not enter on the present tense except with the emphatic nun. It was also said it is the lam of oath.

Abu Ali al-Farisi said: this lam is not the one in your saying "inna Zaydan la-qa'imun," but rather the one in your saying "la-aqumanna," and sawfa has taken the place of one of the two emphatic nuns, so it is as if he said: "wa la-yu'tiyannaka."

It was said the meaning is: and Your Lord will surely give you the conquest in this world and the reward in the Hereafter, so you will be pleased.

It was said: the Basin and intercession; it was said a thousand palaces of white pearl whose dust is musk; and other things were said.

The apparent meaning is that He, glorified is He, gives him what pleases him of the goods of this world and the Hereafter, and among the most important of that to him and the most advanced in his regard is the acceptance of his intercession for his community.

﴿alam yajidka yatiman fa-awa﴾ This begins the enumeration of the blessings which Allah, glorified is He, bestowed upon him: that is, He found you an orphan without a father, so He gave you a refuge (ma'wa) to which you retreat. The majority read fa-awa with an alif after the hamza, quadriliteral, from awahu yu'wihi. Abu al-Ashhab read "fa-awa" triliteral, and it is either with the meaning of the quadriliteral, or it is from awa lahu, meaning when he had mercy on him.

From Mujahid, the meaning of the verse: "Did He not find you unique in your nobility, without any equal, so Allah gave you refuge with companions who protect you and surround you," so "yatiman" is from their saying "durrah yatimah" (a unique pearl). This is very far-fetched. The hamza is for denying a negation and establishing the negated in the most emphatic way, as if he said: "He indeed found you an orphan and gave refuge." And "wujud" means knowledge, and "yatiman" is its second object. It was also said it means encountering, and "yatiman" is a circumstantial accusative from its object.

﴿wa wajadaka dallan fa-hada﴾ This is coordinated with the negated present, and it was said it is coordinated with what the preceding speech implies, as we mentioned: that is, He found you an orphan and gave you refuge, and He found you astray and guided you. "Dall" here means heedlessness, as in His saying: ﴿la yadillu rabbi wa la yansa﴾ (﴿My Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾) [Ta-Ha: 52], and as in His saying: ﴿wa in kunta min qablihi lamina al-ghafilin﴾ (﴿And indeed you were before it among the unaware﴾) [Yusuf: 3]. The meaning: He found you unaware of what was intended for you of the matter of prophethood. al-Zajjaj chose this.

It was also said the meaning of dallan: you did not know the Qur'an nor the laws, so He guided you to that.

al-Kalbi, al-Suddi and al-Farra' said: He found you among a people of error (p-1633), so Allah guided them through you.

It was said He found you seeking the qibla, so He guided you to it, as in His saying: ﴿qad nara taqallub wajhika fi al-sama'i fa-lanuwalliyannaka qiblatan tardaha﴾ (﴿We have seen the turning of your face toward the sky, so We shall surely turn you to a qibla that pleases you﴾) [al-Baqarah: 144], and "dall" would mean seeking.

It was said He found you lost among your people, so He guided you to him, and "dall" would mean lost.

It was said He found you loving guidance, so He guided you to it, and "dall" would mean love, as from the poet's saying:

"How strange of Azzah in choosing my estrangement, after the dall (love), while her rope has worn out."

It was said He found you astray in the valleys of Mecca, so He guided you, meaning He returned you to your grandfather Abd al-Muttalib.

﴿wa wajadaka 'a'ilan fa-aghna﴾ That is: He found you poor, having no wealth, so He enriched you. One says 'aala al-rajulu ya'ilu 'ailatan when he became poor, and from it is the saying of Uhayhah ibn al-Jullah:

"The poor does not know when his wealth will come, and the rich does not know when he will become poor."

That is, he will become poor.

al-Kalbi said: fa-aghna: that is, He satisfied you with what He gave you of provision. al-Farra' chose this, saying: because he was not rich through abundance, but Allah, glorified is He, satisfied him with what He gave him, and that is the reality of richness.

al-Akhfash said: 'a'ilan means one who has dependants, and from it is Jarir's saying:

"Allah sent down in the Book an obligation for the wayfarer and for the needy dependant poor."

It was said: fa-aghna by what He opened for you of conquests, and there is consideration in this, because the surah is Meccan. It was said: by the wealth of Khadijah bint Khuwaylid. It was said: He found you poor in proofs and evidences, so He enriched you with them.

The majority read 'a'ilan, and Muhammad ibn al-Sumayfa' and al-Yamani read "'ayyilan" with a doubled, kasra-vowelled ya', like sayyid.

Then He, glorified is He, enjoined him concerning orphans and the poor, saying: ﴿fa-amma al-yatima fa-la taqhar﴾ (﴿As for the orphan, do not oppress him﴾): that is, do not oppress him in any form of oppression, whoever he may be.

Mujahid said: do not belittle the orphan, for you were an orphan.

al-Akhfash said: do not domineer over him with injustice; give him his right and remember your orphanhood.

al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: do not oppress him regarding his property, so that you take his right because of his weakness.

Thus the Arabs used to do regarding the rights of orphans: they took their wealth and wronged them in their rights. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to show kindness to the orphan, treat him well, and enjoin (kindness) toward orphans.

The majority read ﴿fa-la taqhar﴾ with qaf; Ibn Mas'ud, al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi and al-Ashhab al-Uqayli read "takhar" with kaf, and the Arabs interchange qaf and kaf.

al-Nahhas said: it is only said kahara-hu when he was harsh toward him and rough.

It was said qahr is domination, and kahr is rebuke.

Abu Hayyan said: it is a dialect, meaning the reading with kaf is like the reading of the majority, and "al-yatima" is in the accusative by "taqhar."

﴿wa amma al-sa'ila fa-la tanhar﴾ (﴿And as for the one who asks, do not repel him﴾). One says nahara-hu and intahara-hu when one confronts him with words that rebuke him. So it is a prohibition from rebuking the beggar and being harsh toward him, but rather one gives him a little or returns him with kindness.

al-Wahidi said: the exegetes said: he means the beggar at the door; say: do not rebuke him when he asks you, for you were poor, so either feed him or return him with gentle refusal.

Qatadah said: its meaning: "Return the beggar with mercy and gentleness."

وقيل: المراد بالسائل الذي يسأل عن الدين، فلا تنهره بالغلظة والجفوة، وأجبه برفق ولين. كذا قال سفيان، والسائلَ منصوب بـ(تنهر)، والتقدير: مهما يكن من شيء فلا تقهر اليتيم ولا تنهر السائل.

﴿وأما بنعمة ربك فحدِّث﴾ أمره سبحانه بالتحدث بنعم الله عليه، وإظهارها للناس، وإشهارها بينهم. والظاهر أن النعمة على العموم من غير تخصيص بفرد من أفرادها أو نوع من أنواعها.

وقال مجاهد والكلبي: المراد بالنعمة هنا القرآن.
قال الكلبي: وكان القرآن أعظم ما أنعم الله به عليه، فأمره أن يقرأه.
قال الفراء: وكان يقرؤه ويحدِّث به.

وقال مجاهد أيضًا: المراد بالنعمة النبوةُ التي أعطاها الله. واختار هذا الزجاج فقال: أي بلِّغ ما أُرسلتَ به، وحدِّث بالنبوة التي آتاك الله، وهي أجلّ النعم.

وقال مقاتل: يعني: اشكر ما ذُكر من النعمة عليك في هذه السورة من الهدى بعد الضلالة، وجبر اليتم، والإغناء بعد العيلة، فاشكر هذه النعم.

والتحدث بنعمة الله شكرٌ. والجار والمجرور متعلق بـ(حدِّث)، والفاء غير مانعة من تعلقه به. وهذه النواهي لرسول الله ﷺ هي نواهٍ له ولأمته، لأنهم أسوته، فكل فرد من أفراد هذه الأمة منهيٌّ بكل فرد من أفراد هذه النواهي.

وقد أخرج ابن جرير عن ابن عباس ﴿والليل إذا سجى﴾ قال: إذا أقبل.
وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، وابن مردويه عنه ﴿إذا سجى﴾ قال: إذا ذهب. ﴿ما ودعك ربك﴾ قال: ما تركك. ﴿وما قلى﴾ قال: ما أبغضك.

وأخرج الطبراني في الأوسط، والبيهقي في الدلائل عنه أيضًا قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «عُرض عليَّ ما هو مفتوح لأمتي بعدي، فأنزل الله ﴿ولَلْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَكَ مِنَ الأُولى﴾».

وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة، وعبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، والطبراني، والحاكم وصححه، وابن مردويه، والبيهقي، وأبو نعيم عنه أيضًا قال: «عُرض على رسول الله ﷺ ما هو مفتوح على أمته من بعده، فسُرّ بذلك، فأنزل الله ﴿ولَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضى﴾، فأعطاه في الجنة ألف قصر من لؤلؤ، ترابه المسك، في كل قصر ما ينبغي له من الأزواج والخدم». وأخرج البيهقي في الشعب عن ابن عباس في قوله: ﴿ولَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضى﴾ قال: رضاه أن يدخل أمتَه كلُّهم الجنة.

وأخرج ابن جرير عنه أيضًا في الآية قال: من رضا محمد أن لا يدخل أحدٌ من أهل بيته النار.

وأخرج الخطيب في التلخيص من وجه آخر عنه أيضًا في الآية قال: لا يرضى محمد وأحدٌ من أمته في النار. ويدل على هذا ما أخرجه مسلم عن ابن عمرو «أن النبي ﷺ تلا قولَ الله في إبراهيم ﴿فمن تبعني فإنه مني﴾ وقولَ عيسى ﴿إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك﴾ الآية، فرفع يديه وقال: اللهم أمتي أمتي، وبكى، فقال الله: يا جبريل اذهب إلى محمد فقل له: إنا سنرضيك في أمتك ولا نسوؤك».

وأخرج ابن المنذر، وابن مردويه، وأبو نعيم في الحلية من طريق «حرب بن شريح قال: قلتُ لأبي جعفر محمدِ بن علي بن الحسين: أرأيت هذه الشفاعة التي يتحدث بها أهل العراق، أحقٌّ هي؟ قال: إي والله. حدثني محمد ابن الحنفية عن علي أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: أشفع لأمتي حتى ينادِيَني ربي: أرضيتَ يا محمد؟ فأقول: نعم يا رب رضيت». ثم أقبل علي فقال: إنكم تقولون يا معشرَ (p-١٦٣٤) أهلِ العراق: إن أرجى آية في كتاب الله ﴿يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعًا﴾ [الزمر: ٥٣]. قلتُ: إنا لنقول ذلك. قال: فكنا أهلَ البيت نقول: إن أرجى آية في كتاب الله ﴿ولَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضى﴾ وهي الشفاعة».

وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة عن ابن مسعود قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «إنا أهلَ البيت اختار الله لنا الآخرةَ على الدنيا، ﴿ولَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضى﴾».

وأخرج العسكري في المواعظ، وابن مردويه، وابن النجار عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: «دخل رسول الله ﷺ على فاطمة وهي تطحن بالرحى، وعليها كساء من جلد الإبل، فلما نظر إليها قال: يا فاطمة، تعجّلي مرارةَ الدنيا بنعيم الآخرة، فأنزل الله ﴿ولَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضى﴾».

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، والطبراني، والحاكم وصححه، وابن مردويه، والبيهقي، وأبو نعيم، وابن عساكر عن ابن عباس أن النبي ﷺ قال: «سألتُ ربي مسألةً ودِدتُ أني لم أكن سألتُه، قلت: قد كانت قبلي أنبياءُ منهم من سخرتَ له الريح، ومنهم من كان يحيي الموتى، فقال تعالى: يا محمد، ألم أجدك يتيمًا فآويتُك؟ ألم أجدك ضالًّا فهديتُك؟ ألم أجدك عائلًا فأغنيتُك؟ ألم أشرح لك صدرَك؟ ألم أضع عنك وزرَك؟ ألم أرفع لك ذكرَك؟ قلتُ: بلى يا رب».

وأخرج ابن مردويه عن ابن عباس قال: «لما نزلت ﴿والضحى﴾ على رسول الله ﷺ قال رسول الله ﷺ: يَمُنُّ عليَّ ربي، وأهلٌ أن يَمُنَّ ربي».

وأخرج ابن مردويه عنه في قوله: ﴿ووجدك ضالًّا فهدى﴾ قال: وجدك بين الضالين فاستنقذك من ضلالتهم.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن الحسن بن علي في قوله: ﴿وأما بنعمة ربك فحدِّث﴾ قال: ما علِمتَ من الخير.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عنه في الآية قال: إذا أصبتَ خيرًا فحدِّث إخوانَك.

وأخرج عبد الله بن أحمد في زوائد المسند، والبيهقي في الشعب، والخطيب في المتفق، قال السيوطي: بسند ضعيف، عن النعمان بن بشير قال: «قال رسول الله ﷺ على المنبر: مَن لم يشكر القليل لم يشكر الكثير، ومن لم يشكر الناس لم يشكر الله، والتحدث بنعمة الله شكر، وتركها كفر، والجماعة رحمة».

وأخرج أبو داود، والترمذي وحسّنه، وأبو يعلى، وابن حبان، والبيهقي، والضياء عن جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي ﷺ قال: «مَن أبلى بلاءً فذكره فقد شكره، وإن كتمه فقد كفره». وأخرج البخاري في الأدب، وأبو داود، والضياء عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «مَن أُعطي عطاءً فوجد فليجزِ به، فإن لم يجد فليُثنِ به، فمن أثنى به فقد شكره، ومن كتمه فقد كفره، ومن تحلّى بما لم يُعطَ فإنه كلابس ثوبَيْ زور».

وأخرج أحمد، والطبراني في الأوسط، والبيهقي عن عائشة قالت: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «مَن أُولي معروفًا فليكافئ به، فإن لم يستطع فليذكره، فإن من ذكره فقد شكره».

This surah is Meccan, without any dispute.

Ibn al-Durays, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas: "It was revealed when al-Duha (the forenoon) was in Mecca."

al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated through Abu al-Hasan al-Muqri, who said: I heard Ikrimah ibn Sulayman say: "I recited to Isma'il ibn Qustutin, and when I reached 'Wal-Duha' (﴿Wal-Duha﴾) he said: 'Glorify (takbir) until you finish.' 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir informed him that he had recited to Mujahid, and he ordered him to do so."

Mujahid informed him that Ibn Abbas had ordered him to do so.

Ibn Abbas informed him that Ubayy ibn Ka'b had ordered him to do so.

Ubayy informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had ordered him to do so.

Abu al-Hasan al-Muqri mentioned above is Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Bazzah al-Muqri.

Ibn Kathir said: "This is a sunnah which Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Bazzi, from the descendants of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, was alone in narrating. He was an imam in the readings (qira'at)."

As for in hadith, Abu Hatim al-Razi weakened him and said: "I did not take from him." Likewise Abu Ja'far al-cUqayli said: "He is munkar al-hadith (rejected in narration)."

Ibn Kathir said: "Then the reciters differed about the place of this takbir and its manner. Some of them said: it is glorified from the end of the night when it covers (wa'l-layli idha yaghsha); others said: from the end of al-Duha."

The manner of the takbir according to some of them is that one says: "Allahu akbar" and stops. Among them are those who say: "Allahu akbar, la ilaha illa Allah, Allahu akbar."

They mention, regarding the occasion of the takbir from the beginning of al-Duha, that when revelation was delayed from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and paused for that period, then the angel came and revealed to him "Wal-Duha, wal-layli idha saja" (the surah), and he glorified (Allah) out of joy and happiness. But they did not narrate this with a chain by which it can be judged sound or weak.

al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Jundub al-Bajali, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ fell ill and did not rise for the night for two or three nights. A woman came to him and said: 'O Muhammad, I do not see your devil except that he has left you; he has not come near you for two or three nights.' So Allah revealed: 'Wal-Duha, wal-layli idha saja, ma wadda'aka rabbuka wa ma qala' (﴿Wal-Duha﴾ ﴿wal-layli idha saja﴾ ﴿ma wadda'aka rabbuka wa ma qala﴾)."

al-Firyabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Jundub, who said: "Jibril was delayed from the Prophet ﷺ, so the polytheists said: 'Muhammad has been abandoned,' and then there was revealed: 'Ma wadda'aka rabbuka wa ma qala' (﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He become displeased.﴾)."

al-Tabarani narrated from Jundub, who said: "Jibril was held back from the Prophet ﷺ, and some of his paternal cousins' daughters said: 'I do not see your companion except that he has become displeased with you,' so there was revealed: 'Wal-Duha' (﴿By the morning brightness﴾)."

al-Tirmidhi, who declared it sound, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Jundub, and in it: a woman said to him: "I do not see your devil except that he has left you," so there was revealed: "Wal-Duha" (p-1632).

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Here al-Duha means the whole of the daytime.

Due to His saying: ﴿wal-layli idha saja﴾ (﴿By the night when it covers﴾). When He contrasted al-Duha with the night, this indicates that what is meant by it is the entire day, not part of it.

It is in origin a name for the time when the sun rises high, as was mentioned earlier in His saying: ﴿wash-shamsi wa duhaha﴾ (﴿By the sun and its brightness﴾). The apparent meaning is that what is meant is al-Duha without specification.

Qatadah, Muqatil and Ja'far al-Sadiq said: what is meant by it is the forenoon in which Allah spoke to Musa, and what is meant by His saying ﴿wal-layli idha saja﴾ is the night of the Mi'raj. It was also said that what is meant by al-Duha is the hour in which the magicians fell down prostrating, as in His saying: ﴿wa an yuhsharan-nasu duha﴾ (﴿and that the people be gathered in the forenoon﴾) [Ta-Ha: 59]. It was also said that the sworn-by thing has an implied omitted noun, as was mentioned earlier in its parallels: that is, "by the Lord of al-Duha." It was also said its estimate is: "and by the brightness of al-Duha," but there is no basis for this, for Allah the Exalted may swear by whatever He wills of His creation. It was also said: al-Duha is the light of Paradise and al-layl is the darkness of Hell; it was also said al-Duha is the light of the hearts of the knowers and al-layl is the blackness of the hearts of the disbelievers.

﴿wal-layli idha saja﴾ means: became still. Thus said Qatadah, Mujahid, Ibn Zayd, Ikrimah and others: one says "laylatun sajiyah," meaning a still night, and one says of an eye when its gaze becomes still that it is sajiyah. One says: saja al-shay'u yasju sujuwwan, when it became still.

Ata said: saja means when it was covered with majesty.

Thalab narrated from Ibn al-A'rabi: saja means its darkness extended.

al-Asma'i said: the sujuww of the night is its covering of the day, like a man being covered with a garment.

al-Hasan said: it covered with its darkness.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it came forward.

Mujahid also said: it leveled out. The first is preferable, and it is the view of the majority of the exegetes and the lexicographers.

The meaning of its stillness is the settling and leveling of its darkness, so that nothing is added to it after that.

﴿ma wadda'aka rabbuka﴾ This is the answer to the oath: that is, your Lord has not cut you off as one who bids farewell. The majority read ﴿ma wadda'aka﴾ with the dal doubled, from tawdi' (bidding farewell), which is the farewell of one departing. Ibn Abbas, Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Ibn Hashim, Ibn Abi Ablah and Abu Haywah read it with the dal lightened, from their saying wada'ahu, meaning he left him. From this is the poet's saying:

"Ask my amir what changed him from my union today, until he left him."

Tawdi' is more emphatic in farewell, for whoever bids you farewell while departing has gone far in abandoning you.

al-Mubarrad said: they hardly say wada'a nor wadhara, because of the weakness of the waw when it is put first, and they dispensed with it by tarak (he left).

Abu Ubayda said: wadda'aka is from tawdi', as one who bids farewell takes leave.

al-Zajjaj said: He did not cut off the revelation. We have already mentioned the cause of revelation of this verse at the beginning of this surah.

﴿wa ma qala﴾ al-qila means hatred; one says qalahu, yaqlihi, qila'.

al-Zajjaj said: and He did not hate you. He said ﴿wa ma qala﴾ and did not say wa ma qalaka, for agreement with the ends of the verses. The meaning: and He did not hate you. From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

"I am not one who hates the friends, nor one who hates."

﴿wa lal-akhiratu khayrun laka mina al-ula﴾ The lam is the answer to a omitted oath: that is, Paradise is better for you than this world, even though he ﷺ was given in this world of the nobility of prophethood what makes every nobility small in comparison and every honour in this world diminish in relation to it. But since this world in its entirety is mixed with troubles and disturbed by human accidents, and life in it is like the dreams of a sleeper or a passing shadow, it is nothing in relation to the Hereafter; and since it is a path to the Hereafter and a cause of attaining what Allah has prepared for His righteous servants of great good, through the deeds performed in it which necessitate winning Paradise, it has some good in it in general from this aspect.

﴿wa la-sawfa yu'tika rabbuka fa-tarda﴾ This lam — it was said it is the lam of the beginning, entering on the predicate to emphasize the content of the sentence, and the subject is omitted, its estimate being "wa la-anta sawfa yu'tika" etc. It is not the lam of oath, because it does not enter on the present tense except with the emphatic nun. It was also said it is the lam of oath.

Abu Ali al-Farisi said: this lam is not the one in your saying "inna Zaydan la-qa'imun," but rather the one in your saying "la-aqumanna," and sawfa has taken the place of one of the two emphatic nuns, so it is as if he said: "wa la-yu'tiyannaka."

It was said the meaning is: and Your Lord will surely give you the conquest in this world and the reward in the Hereafter, so you will be pleased.

It was said: the Basin and intercession; it was said a thousand palaces of white pearl whose dust is musk; and other things were said.

The apparent meaning is that He, glorified is He, gives him what pleases him of the goods of this world and the Hereafter, and among the most important of that to him and the most advanced in his regard is the acceptance of his intercession for his community.

﴿alam yajidka yatiman fa-awa﴾ This begins the enumeration of the blessings which Allah, glorified is He, bestowed upon him: that is, He found you an orphan without a father, so He gave you a refuge (ma'wa) to which you retreat. The majority read fa-awa with an alif after the hamza, quadriliteral, from awahu yu'wihi. Abu al-Ashhab read "fa-awa" triliteral, and it is either with the meaning of the quadriliteral, or it is from awa lahu, meaning when he had mercy on him.

From Mujahid, the meaning of the verse: "Did He not find you unique in your nobility, without any equal, so Allah gave you refuge with companions who protect you and surround you," so "yatiman" is from their saying "durrah yatimah" (a unique pearl). This is very far-fetched. The hamza is for denying a negation and establishing the negated in the most emphatic way, as if he said: "He indeed found you an orphan and gave refuge." And "wujud" means knowledge, and "yatiman" is its second object. It was also said it means encountering, and "yatiman" is a circumstantial accusative from its object.

﴿wa wajadaka dallan fa-hada﴾ This is coordinated with the negated present, and it was said it is coordinated with what the preceding speech implies, as we mentioned: that is, He found you an orphan and gave you refuge, and He found you astray and guided you. "Dall" here means heedlessness, as in His saying: ﴿la yadillu rabbi wa la yansa﴾ (﴿My Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾) [Ta-Ha: 52], and as in His saying: ﴿wa in kunta min qablihi lamina al-ghafilin﴾ (﴿And indeed you were before it among the unaware﴾) [Yusuf: 3]. The meaning: He found you unaware of what was intended for you of the matter of prophethood. al-Zajjaj chose this.

It was also said the meaning of dallan: you did not know the Qur'an nor the laws, so He guided you to that.

al-Kalbi, al-Suddi and al-Farra' said: He found you among a people of error (p-1633), so Allah guided them through you.

It was said He found you seeking the qibla, so He guided you to it, as in His saying: ﴿qad nara taqallub wajhika fi al-sama'i fa-lanuwalliyannaka qiblatan tardaha﴾ (﴿We have seen the turning of your face toward the sky, so We shall surely turn you to a qibla that pleases you﴾) [al-Baqarah: 144], and "dall" would mean seeking.

It was said He found you lost among your people, so He guided you to him, and "dall" would mean lost.

It was said He found you loving guidance, so He guided you to it, and "dall" would mean love, as from the poet's saying:

"How strange of Azzah in choosing my estrangement, after the dall (love), while her rope has worn out."

It was said He found you astray in the valleys of Mecca, so He guided you, meaning He returned you to your grandfather Abd al-Muttalib.

﴿wa wajadaka 'a'ilan fa-aghna﴾ That is: He found you poor, having no wealth, so He enriched you. One says 'aala al-rajulu ya'ilu 'ailatan when he became poor, and from it is the saying of Uhayhah ibn al-Jullah:

"The poor does not know when his wealth will come, and the rich does not know when he will become poor."

That is, he will become poor.

al-Kalbi said: fa-aghna: that is, He satisfied you with what He gave you of provision. al-Farra' chose this, saying: because he was not rich through abundance, but Allah, glorified is He, satisfied him with what He gave him, and that is the reality of richness.

al-Akhfash said: 'a'ilan means one who has dependants, and from it is Jarir's saying:

"Allah sent down in the Book an obligation for the wayfarer and for the needy dependant poor."

It was said: fa-aghna by what He opened for you of conquests, and there is consideration in this, because the surah is Meccan. It was said: by the wealth of Khadijah bint Khuwaylid. It was said: He found you poor in proofs and evidences, so He enriched you with them.

The majority read 'a'ilan, and Muhammad ibn al-Sumayfa' and al-Yamani read "'ayyilan" with a doubled, kasra-vowelled ya', like sayyid.

Then He, glorified is He, enjoined him concerning orphans and the poor, saying: ﴿fa-amma al-yatima fa-la taqhar﴾ (﴿As for the orphan, do not oppress him﴾): that is, do not oppress him in any form of oppression, whoever he may be.

Mujahid said: do not belittle the orphan, for you were an orphan.

al-Akhfash said: do not domineer over him with injustice; give him his right and remember your orphanhood.

al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: do not oppress him regarding his property, so that you take his right because of his weakness.

Thus the Arabs used to do regarding the rights of orphans: they took their wealth and wronged them in their rights. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to show kindness to the orphan, treat him well, and enjoin (kindness) toward orphans.

The majority read ﴿fa-la taqhar﴾ with qaf; Ibn Mas'ud, al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi and al-Ashhab al-Uqayli read "takhar" with kaf, and the Arabs interchange qaf and kaf.

al-Nahhas said: it is only said kahara-hu when he was harsh toward him and rough.

It was said qahr is domination, and kahr is rebuke.

Abu Hayyan said: it is a dialect, meaning the reading with kaf is like the reading of the majority, and "al-yatima" is in the accusative by "taqhar."

﴿wa amma al-sa'ila fa-la tanhar﴾ (﴿And as for the one who asks, do not repel him﴾). One says nahara-hu and intahara-hu when one confronts him with words that rebuke him. So it is a prohibition from rebuking the beggar and being harsh toward him, but rather one gives him a little or returns him with kindness.

al-Wahidi said: the exegetes said: he means the beggar at the door; say: do not rebuke him when he asks you, for you were poor, so either feed him or return him with gentle refusal.

Qatadah said: its meaning: "Return the beggar with mercy and gentleness."

وقيل: المراد بالسائل الذي يسأل عن الدين، فلا تنهره بالغلظة والجفوة، وأجبه برفق ولين. كذا قال سفيان، والسائلَ منصوب بـ(تنهر)، والتقدير: مهما يكن من شيء فلا تقهر اليتيم ولا تنهر السائل.

﴿وأما بنعمة ربك فحدِّث﴾ أمره سبحانه بالتحدث بنعم الله عليه، وإظهارها للناس، وإشهارها بينهم. والظاهر أن النعمة على العموم من غير تخصيص بفرد من أفرادها أو نوع من أنواعها.

وقال مجاهد والكلبي: المراد بالنعمة هنا القرآن.
قال الكلبي: وكان القرآن أعظم ما أنعم الله به عليه، فأمره أن يقرأه.
قال الفراء: وكان يقرؤه ويحدِّث به.

وقال مجاهد أيضًا: المراد بالنعمة النبوةُ التي أعطاها الله. واختار هذا الزجاج فقال: أي بلِّغ ما أُرسلتَ به، وحدِّث بالنبوة التي آتاك الله، وهي أجلّ النعم.

وقال مقاتل: يعني: اشكر ما ذُكر من النعمة عليك في هذه السورة من الهدى بعد الضلالة، وجبر اليتم، والإغناء بعد العيلة، فاشكر هذه النعم.

والتحدث بنعمة الله شكرٌ. والجار والمجرور متعلق بـ(حدِّث)، والفاء غير مانعة من تعلقه به. وهذه النواهي لرسول الله ﷺ هي نواهٍ له ولأمته، لأنهم أسوته، فكل فرد من أفراد هذه الأمة منهيٌّ بكل فرد من أفراد هذه النواهي.

وقد أخرج ابن جرير عن ابن عباس ﴿والليل إذا سجى﴾ قال: إذا أقبل.
وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، وابن مردويه عنه ﴿إذا سجى﴾ قال: إذا ذهب. ﴿ما ودعك ربك﴾ قال: ما تركك. ﴿وما قلى﴾ قال: ما أبغضك.

وأخرج الطبراني في الأوسط، والبيهقي في الدلائل عنه أيضًا قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «عُرض عليَّ ما هو مفتوح لأمتي بعدي، فأنزل الله ﴿ولَلْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَكَ مِنَ الأُولى﴾».

وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة، وعبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، والطبراني، والحاكم وصححه، وابن مردويه، والبيهقي، وأبو نعيم عنه أيضًا قال: «عُرض على رسول الله ﷺ ما هو مفتوح على أمته من بعده، فسُرّ بذلك، فأنزل الله ﴿ولَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضى﴾، فأعطاه في الجنة ألف قصر من لؤلؤ، ترابه المسك، في كل قصر ما ينبغي له من الأزواج والخدم». وأخرج البيهقي في الشعب عن ابن عباس في قوله: ﴿ولَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضى﴾ قال: رضاه أن يدخل أمتَه كلُّهم الجنة.

وأخرج ابن جرير عنه أيضًا في الآية قال: من رضا محمد أن لا يدخل أحدٌ من أهل بيته النار.

وأخرج الخطيب في التلخيص من وجه آخر عنه أيضًا في الآية قال: لا يرضى محمد وأحدٌ من أمته في النار. ويدل على هذا ما أخرجه مسلم عن ابن عمرو «أن النبي ﷺ تلا قولَ الله في إبراهيم ﴿فمن تبعني فإنه مني﴾ وقولَ عيسى ﴿إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك﴾ الآية، فرفع يديه وقال: اللهم أمتي أمتي، وبكى، فقال الله: يا جبريل اذهب إلى محمد فقل له: إنا سنرضيك في أمتك ولا نسوؤك».

وأخرج ابن المنذر، وابن مردويه، وأبو نعيم في الحلية من طريق «حرب بن شريح قال: قلتُ لأبي جعفر محمدِ بن علي بن الحسين: أرأيت هذه الشفاعة التي يتحدث بها أهل العراق، أحقٌّ هي؟ قال: إي والله. حدثني محمد ابن الحنفية عن علي أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: أشفع لأمتي حتى ينادِيَني ربي: أرضيتَ يا محمد؟ فأقول: نعم يا رب رضيت». ثم أقبل علي فقال: إنكم تقولون يا معشرَ (p-١٦٣٤) أهلِ العراق: إن أرجى آية في كتاب الله ﴿يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعًا﴾ [الزمر: ٥٣]. قلتُ: إنا لنقول ذلك. قال: فكنا أهلَ البيت نقول: إن أرجى آية في كتاب الله ﴿ولَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضى﴾ وهي الشفاعة».

وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة عن ابن مسعود قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «إنا أهلَ البيت اختار الله لنا الآخرةَ على الدنيا، ﴿ولَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضى﴾».

وأخرج العسكري في المواعظ، وابن مردويه، وابن النجار عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: «دخل رسول الله ﷺ على فاطمة وهي تطحن بالرحى، وعليها كساء من جلد الإبل، فلما نظر إليها قال: يا فاطمة، تعجّلي مرارةَ الدنيا بنعيم الآخرة، فأنزل الله ﴿ولَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضى﴾».

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، والطبراني، والحاكم وصححه، وابن مردويه، والبيهقي، وأبو نعيم، وابن عساكر عن ابن عباس أن النبي ﷺ قال: «سألتُ ربي مسألةً ودِدتُ أني لم أكن سألتُه، قلت: قد كانت قبلي أنبياءُ منهم من سخرتَ له الريح، ومنهم من كان يحيي الموتى، فقال تعالى: يا محمد، ألم أجدك يتيمًا فآويتُك؟ ألم أجدك ضالًّا فهديتُك؟ ألم أجدك عائلًا فأغنيتُك؟ ألم أشرح لك صدرَك؟ ألم أضع عنك وزرَك؟ ألم أرفع لك ذكرَك؟ قلتُ: بلى يا رب».

وأخرج ابن مردويه عن ابن عباس قال: «لما نزلت ﴿والضحى﴾ على رسول الله ﷺ قال رسول الله ﷺ: يَمُنُّ عليَّ ربي، وأهلٌ أن يَمُنَّ ربي».

وأخرج ابن مردويه عنه في قوله: ﴿ووجدك ضالًّا فهدى﴾ قال: وجدك بين الضالين فاستنقذك من ضلالتهم.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن الحسن بن علي في قوله: ﴿وأما بنعمة ربك فحدِّث﴾ قال: ما علِمتَ من الخير.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عنه في الآية قال: إذا أصبتَ خيرًا فحدِّث إخوانَك.

وأخرج عبد الله بن أحمد في زوائد المسند، والبيهقي في الشعب، والخطيب في المتفق، قال السيوطي: بسند ضعيف، عن النعمان بن بشير قال: «قال رسول الله ﷺ على المنبر: مَن لم يشكر القليل لم يشكر الكثير، ومن لم يشكر الناس لم يشكر الله، والتحدث بنعمة الله شكر، وتركها كفر، والجماعة رحمة».

وأخرج أبو داود، والترمذي وحسّنه، وأبو يعلى، وابن حبان، والبيهقي، والضياء عن جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي ﷺ قال: «مَن أبلى بلاءً فذكره فقد شكره، وإن كتمه فقد كفره». وأخرج البخاري في الأدب، وأبو داود، والضياء عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «مَن أُعطي عطاءً فوجد فليجزِ به، فإن لم يجد فليُثنِ به، فمن أثنى به فقد شكره، ومن كتمه فقد كفره، ومن تحلّى بما لم يُعطَ فإنه كلابس ثوبَيْ زور».

وأخرج أحمد، والطبراني في الأوسط، والبيهقي عن عائشة قالت: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «مَن أُولي معروفًا فليكافئ به، فإن لم يستطع فليذكره، فإن من ذكره فقد شكره».

This surah is Meccan, without any dispute.

Ibn al-Durays, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas: "It was revealed when al-Duha (the forenoon) was in Mecca."
